newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expects to meet with Yeltsin in March.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expects to meet with Yeltsin in March.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday he expects to meet in March with Russian President Boris Yeltsin as planned, although officials said the summit might be in a third country due to the Kremlin leader's health.
A senior administration official said there was a "strong possibility" the meeting now set for the United States would be held elsewhere to ease the travel strain on Yeltsin.

"We have a huge, full agenda," Clinton said of his scheduled summit with Yeltsin. "And we have been given no impression by the Russians that we aren't still going to have the Yeltsin-Clinton meeting in the March timeframe."
Yeltsin, looking alert and smiling, appeared on Russian television on Tuesday for the first time in three weeks in a bid to calm concerns about his long-term health and his ability to govern.
He was shown talking with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who will be in Washington next week for talks with Vice President Al Gore that include finalising details of the summit.
The administration official, who spoke on condition he not be identified, said a "meeting in a third country is a strong possiblity ... although the United States has not been ruled out."
Clinton, during a White House news conference, stressed that the meeting was "very important," noting the various economic and security issues on the agenda.

He cited several issues that need to be dealt with -- including the expansion of NATO, which Moscow sees as a security threat, and Washington's desire for Yeltsin to press for ratification of the START II treaty on reducing both nation's nuclear arsenals.
"So I think we'll go right on, and I expect to have that meeting in March," Clinton said. "And I expect it to be an important one and, I hope, a successful one."
Clinton's comments washed away earlier comments by administration officials who suggested that the summit might have to be delayed because of Yeltsin's health problems.
The 65-year-old Yeltsin had quintuple bypass surgery Nov. 5 and fell ill earlier this month to double pneumonia -- touching off debate in parliament over whether he should resign.
In his news conference, Clinton stressed that he had "no private information that is inconsistent with the public statements of the Russian government on President Yeltsin's health."
"I have no reason to believe, based on any information I have, that his condition is any different from what the Russian government has said it is," Clinton said.

Yeltsin on Monday cancelled a planned trip to the Netherlands on the recommendation of his doctors, who said he should not fly until fully recovered from pneumonia. He is slated to meet on Monday in Moscow with French President Jacques Chirac.

White House officials stress that no specific date has been set for the summit, nor has any site been determined. Under normal situations, Yeltsin would travel to the United States because he hosted the last summit, in Moscow in April.
